newsitem.title: USA: Citicorp consumer credit costs up in Q4.
newsitem.headline: Citicorp consumer credit costs up in Q4.

text.p: Citicorp said Tuesday that consumer credit costs rose to $844 million in the 1996 fourth quarter from $688 million a year earlier.
The ratio of net credit losses to average managed loans was 2.51 percent in the fourth quarter, up from 2.14 percent a year earlier, it said. The increase came in credit cards, it said.
Its Citibanking and private bank credit costs improved in the quarter, it said.

Citicorp said credit costs in its U.S. bankcard business continued to rise in the fourth quarter. The chargeoff rate was 5.45 percent of average managed loans, compared to 5.11 percent in the 1996 third quarter and 3.89 percent, adjusted for the sale of bankrupt accounts, in the 1995 fourth quarter.
Bankruptcies represented 38.0 percent of gross U.S. bankcard writeoffs in the fourth quarter, compared with 37.5 percent in the 1996 third quarter and 35.6 percent in the 1995 fourth quarter.

Credit costs in cards portfolios other than U.S. bankcards, which include emerging markets and developed markets of Europe and Japan, and the worldwide Diners Club business, were $77 million, or 3.58 percent of average loans in the fourth quarter, down from $89 million, or 4.35 percent, in the third quarter, and $82 million, or 4.59 percent, in the 1995 fourth quarter. Citicorp said the decrease mainly reflected continued improvement in Latin America.

Fourth-quarter revenue in the emerging markets cards business rose 27 percent from a year ago, reflecting continued growth in Asia Pacific and Middle East businesses, and improvements in Latin America including Credicard, a Brazilian affiliate.

Card revenue of $1.8 billion in the fourth quarter rose 13 percent from a year earlier. U.S. bankcard revenue rose 12 percent, reflecting growth in managed receivables, which were up $2.1 billion or five percent from a year ago to $47.0 billion at the end of December. The revenue increase also reflected spread improvement.

Net income from cards worldwide fell to $290 million in the fourth quarter, a decrease of $74 million, or 20 percent, from a year ago, reflecting the continued increase in U.S. bankcard credit losses. The fourth quarter net income in cards was a 19 percent improvement from the third quarter of 1996, primarily due to higher earnings in emerging markets.
Corporate banking net income rose to $549 million in the fourth quarter from $430 million a year ago. Corporate banking revenue rose 26 percent to $2.0 billion.
Emerging markets net income in the fourth quarter was $295 million, an eight percent increase from a year ago.
Citicorp said its effective tax rate was 38 percent in the fourth quarter, up from 37 percent a year ago. For the full years, the effective tax rate was 38 percent for both 1996 and 1995.
